title: Buying Down Your Home Loan Interest Rate

faqs.q: What does it mean to buy down a mortgage interest rate?
faqs.a: Buying down your interest rate means paying a one-time fee upfront at the time you take out your loan to secure a lower mortgage rate. The lender or broker charges a fee known as a discount point to apply this rate reduction.

faqs.q: How much does a mortgage discount point cost and how much does it lower the rate?
faqs.a: One discount point is equal to 1% of your total loan amount. For example, on a $200,000 mortgage, one point costs $2,000. Paying one full discount point typically lowers your ongoing interest rate by approximately a quarter of a percent (0.25%).

faqs.q: What is the difference between a simple buydown and a temporary structured buydown?
faqs.a: A simple mortgage buydown lowers your interest rate for the entire life of the loan and is available for Conventional, FHA, VA, and USDA options. In contrast, structured temporary options like a 2-1 or 3-2-1 buydown offer a significantly lower rate initially, which then increases by 1% each year for the first two or three years before locking into a fixed rate for the remaining term.

faqs.q: Can you get a seller to pay for your interest rate buydown points?
faqs.a: Yes, you can negotiate in your purchase contract to have the seller pay for your buydown points, subject to lender approval guidelines. Notably, these buydown points remain tax-deductible for the homebuyer in the year the loan closes, even if the seller pays for them on your behalf.
